items.q: What did the bank say it certifies?
items.a: **Applications, not models**: a model's benchmark score doesn't prove an app is ready.

items.q: Why don't public benchmarks settle it?
items.a: They test **open data**, not **your data and use case**.

items.q: What three deployment requirements do banks have?

items.a: A **golden dataset** of inputs, expected outputs and metadata, treated like **QA test cases**.

items.q: What do runs against the golden set produce?
items.a: **Traces** that serve as **evidence** for each score.

items.q: How should each dimension be scored?
items.a: A blend of **deterministic scorers**, **path checks** and **LLM judges**, not judges alone.

items.q: How did numeric accuracy go from 60% to about 95%?
items.a: By giving the agent a **deterministic calculate tool** instead of doing math itself.

items.q: Why can an app with a great average still fail?
items.a: **Regulatory compliance is binary**; a zero there **shuts the gate**.

items.q: Who should set the pass thresholds?
items.a: **Domain and risk experts**, per use case and per dimension.
